tasks.commitMessage: test(sync): end-to-end offline create -> reachable remote -> topo arrives

risks: AUDIT CORRECTION, load-bearing: the spec's S8 claims `dirty` is "written `true` by every repository". It is NOT. `grep -rn dirty lib --include="*.dart" | grep -v app_database.g.dart` shows 30 `dirty: const Value(true)` writes, but 15 push-worthy writes omit it entirely — `LibraryCrudRepository._insertArea`/`renameArea`/`_insertSector`/`renameSector`/`createWall`/`renameWall`/`attachPhotoToWall` and ALL FIVE Area/Sector/Wall/Photo/Route tombstone writes in the soft-delete cascade, plus all three `RouteRepository` writes (`upsertRoute` insert + update, `softDeleteRoute`). Gating the push on `dirty` without T3 would silently stop syncing every create, every rename, every route edit and most tombstones. T3 must not be skipped or deferred.

1d MUST LAND BEFORE T4. `SupabaseSyncRemote.upsertOwnRows` (sync_remote.dart:369-400) wraps each table in try/catch and `continue`s with only a `debugPrint`, returning `void` — so "the call did not throw" is currently NOT the same as "the rows landed" (that is exactly S1). T4 clears `dirty` on a non-throwing push, so until 1d makes per-table failure visible, a swallowed table error clears flags for rows that never arrived. Blast radius is bounded by design (the retained `PushScope.full` re-push on app start and on every connectivity regain re-sends everything regardless of flags), but the honest sequencing is 1d first. When 1d lands, narrow T4's clear from `tablesToRows` to `tablesToRows` minus 1d's failed-table set — one call-site change at the `await _clearDirty(tablesToRows);` line.

The (id, updatedAt) compare-and-swap has one narrow accepted hole: two writes to the SAME row within one millisecond share an `updatedAt`, so the second's `dirty` would be cleared by the in-flight push. It needs two distinct user operations on one row inside 1 ms, it is the same resolution `shouldPushLww` already depends on, and the full-scope re-push recovers it. Closing it properly needs a monotonic local revision column, i.e. a schema migration to v9 — deliberately out of scope. Documented in `_clearDirty`'s doc rather than left implicit.

Dirty-scoped push interacts with §1f's photo work. T4 mitigates the obvious hazard by clearing `dirty` only AFTER the byte phase, so a failed upload leaves rows dirty and the retry re-attempts both. But a photo whose row is CLEAN and whose bytes failed on an earlier push is not re-attempted by a `dirtyOnly` push — only by the `PushScope.full` catch-up. §1f-3 ("byte-upload failures are counted and retried through §1e's loop") is where that gets a first-class signal; if §1f lands first, extend `hasPendingLocalChanges()` to include "a photo row whose object is missing remotely" rather than reworking the scope enum.

`fake_async` is deliberately NOT used, contrary to a literal reading of the brief. Three reasons: it is not in `pubspec.yaml` (only a transitive dep via flutter_test), so importing it trips `depend_on_referenced_packages` from `package:flutter_lints`; the orchestrator tests need a real `AppDatabase(NativeDatabase.memory())` for `tableUpdates()`, whose sqlite3 work does not advance under a fake clock; and the entire existing orchestrator suite is built on the shrink-the-seam + tiny-real-delay pattern (`debounce: const Duration(milliseconds: 25)`). The brief's actual requirement — never wait out a production interval — is met and strengthened: the backoff GROWTH LAW is asserted with zero timers in `sync_retry_schedule_test.dart`, and the orchestrator asserts the *requested attempt numbers* via `_RecordingRetrySchedule` rather than measuring wall-clock. If the verifier insists on fake_async, the correct move is adding it to `dev_dependencies` first — a pubspec change that collides with other workstreams.

`ConnectivityService.statusChanges()` is a NEW ABSTRACT MEMBER, so all four existing fakes stop compiling until updated: `test/features/backup/application/sync_orchestrator_test.dart:143`, `test/features/backup/data/sync_service_test.dart:276`, `test/features/backup/data/cloud_backup_service_test.dart:74`, `test/app/app_test.dart:132`. Making it a concrete member with a default body would NOT help — all four use `implements`, which requires every member regardless.

The nastiest trap in T7, and the reason for the plugin-availability probe: `Connectivity.onConnectivityChanged` is an `EventChannel`, and an EventChannel whose plugin is unregistered reports through `FlutterError.reportError`, which `testWidgets` converts into a hard failure that NO `try`/`catch` or `Stream.onError` can intercept. `test/widget_test.dart:79` and `:2119` mount `MasiApp` with only `appDatabaseProvider`/`nowMsProvider` overridden, so without the probe those two tests would start failing the moment the orchestrator subscribes. The `checkConnectivity()` probe (a plain MethodChannel call → catchable `MissingPluginException`) is what keeps widget_test.dart untouched. Do not "simplify" it away.

A confirmed push writes to the DB (`_clearDirty`), which fires `tableUpdates()`, which arms another debounce timer. That follow-up push finds nothing dirty and writes nothing, so the cycle terminates after exactly one extra indexed LIMIT-1 query per table — verified by T6's "the retry loop TERMINATES" test, which asserts the push count stops growing. Anyone changing the nothing-pending early-out must re-run that test or risk a genuine write loop.

`_fullResyncDue` starts `true`, so the first push of every app run is a full-state push even when nothing changed, and web's resume-on-tab-focus makes the first tab-focus pay for it. That is the intended D-4 safety net (once per orchestrator lifetime, plus once per connectivity regain), but it is also S7 cost: with no pagination anywhere, a large library means nine unfiltered selects plus one `inFilter('id', [every id])` per table. If that proves too heavy on device, throttle the regain-triggered full push rather than removing the app-start one.

`SyncPushOutcome` was deliberately NOT extended with a `skippedNothingPending` case, even though it would read better: the orchestrator's pre-flight `hasPendingLocalChanges()` check achieves the same thing without forcing every exhaustive `switch` on that enum to change — which matters because §1d is rewriting `PushSyncResult` in the same file at the same time.

`stripLocalOnlySyncColumns` lives in `sync_remote.dart`, which §1d (upsertOwnRows return type, filterValidSyncRows failure channel) and §1f-4 (paginated object listing) both also edit. It is additive and placed at the end of the top-level-helper block after `filterValidSyncRows`, which minimises but does not eliminate the merge surface.

Docs left stale by this workstream and worth fixing in whichever workstream owns the doc pass: `CLAUDE.md`'s "outbox push/pull" (there is no outbox — `grep -rin outbox lib` is still zero hits after this work) and its "~377 tests" (baseline is 1576). `tables.dart:8`'s `dirty` doc becomes accurate for the first time as of T3/T4 and could usefully gain a pointer to `SyncService.hasPendingLocalChanges`.
sequencingNotes:
HARD ORDERING WITHIN THIS WORKSTREAM: T1 (importSnapshot forces `dirty: false`) MUST precede T2 (strip the columns from the payload) — after T2 a cloud row comes back with no `dirty` key, and `<Table>.fromJson`'s `serializer.fromJson<bool>(json['dirty'])` throws on null, so shipping T2 first red-fails every device-A→device-B round-trip test in `sync_service_test.dart`. T3 (complete the dirty writer surface) MUST precede T4/T6 — see the first risk. T5 must precede T6 (`syncRetryScheduleProvider`), T4 must precede T6 (`PushScope`, `hasPendingLocalChanges`), T7 must precede T8 (`statusChanges()`), and T6 must precede T9 (`pushNow()`). T10 composes everything and must run last.

CROSS-WORKSTREAM FILE COLLISIONS — none of these may run in parallel with 1e (per the repo rule that parallel implementers must be strictly write-disjoint at FILE level):

- `lib/features/backup/application/sync_orchestrator.dart` — shared with §1d (a push that did not land can never produce `idle` + a fresh `lastSyncedAt`; making `SyncStatus.offline` reachable). 1e rewrites `_runPush`'s whole body and adds ~120 lines of fields/methods; 1d rewrites the same `switch (result.outcome)`. Guaranteed conflict. Land 1d first, then 1e's T6 builds on 1d's outcome handling. `SyncRetrySchedule` was deliberately put in its OWN file (`sync_retry_schedule.dart`) to keep that much out of the contested file.
- `lib/features/backup/data/sync_service.dart` — shared with §1d (aggregate a `rowsFailed`/failure channel into `PushSyncResult`; surface `filterValidSyncRows` skips) AND §1f (flip upload order to bytes-then-metadata, count byte failures). All three edit `pushOwn`. 1e changes its signature, its nine snapshot selects, and its tail; 1f reorders that same tail. Serialise: 1d → 1e → 1f, and have 1f rebase onto 1e's `_clearDirty` placement (bytes-before-metadata moves the upload above `upsertOwnRows`, and `_clearDirty` must stay AFTER both).
- `lib/features/backup/data/connectivity_service.dart` — shared with §1d (`SyncStatus.offline` via a real reachability probe to the Supabase origin). 1e adds `statusChanges()` + `classifyConnectivityResults`; 1d likely adds a `probeReachability()`-style member to the same abstract class and the same four test fakes. Serialise, and coordinate so both new members land in one pass over `ConnectivityService`'s four implementers rather than two.
- `lib/features/backup/data/sync_remote.dart` — shared with §1d (`upsertOwnRows` returns per-table outcomes) and §1f-4 (paginate `listPhotoObjectPaths`/`listSharedPhotoObjectPaths`). 1e's change is purely additive (two new top-level helpers after `filterValidSyncRows`), so it is the least contested of the four, but still not parallel-safe.
- `lib/features/library/data/library_crud_repository.dart` — shared with §1c item 4 ("guarded mutations verify their affected row count"), which touches the SAME `_ownOrUnowned`-guarded update statements at :176-183, :278-285, :368-375, :435-448, :1280-1286, :1303-1311 that 1e adds `dirty: const Value(true)` to. High-collision, small-diff-vs-large-diff shape — exactly the situation that previously required a git-stash recovery. Serialise; 1e's T3 is mechanical and fast, so running it first and letting 1c rebase is cheapest.
- `lib/app/app.dart` — 1e only (§1c touches `lib/app/router.dart`, not `app.dart`). Currently uncontested.
- `lib/features/backup/data/backup_repository.dart` — 1e only. Uncontested.

TEST-FILE COLLISIONS (same rule applies): `test/features/backup/data/sync_service_test.dart` is edited by 1d, 1e and 1f; `test/features/backup/application/sync_orchestrator_test.dart` by 1d and 1e; `test/features/backup/data/connectivity_service_test.dart` by 1d and 1e; `test/app/app_test.dart` by 1e (and by 1c if it adds a router/auth-gate widget test there); `test/features/library/data/library_crud_repository_test.dart` by 1c and 1e. Note especially that 1e RESHAPES two shared helpers other workstreams will want to use — `makeContainer` in `sync_orchestrator_test.dart:175-207` gains `connectivityService` and `retrySchedule` parameters and now overrides `connectivityServiceProvider`, and `insertArea` at :209-219 now seeds `dirty: true`.
